description: Low-frequency USD/JPY fundamentals used by the FX carry (S5, scripts/research_fx_carry.py) and FX fundamentals (S6, scripts/research_fx_fundamentals.py) studies: FRED daily/monthly macro series, CFTC Commitments-of-Traders JPY futures positioning, MOF Japan 2-year JGB yields, and MOF's official FX-intervention daily detail. backtest_data/fx_fundamentals_20260822/ is S6's own permanent snapshot (fetched independently of S5's root-level fred_*.csv, by design -- S5 coordinates constants, not data, per research_fx_fundamentals.py).
source: FRED daily CSV (no key, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=<SERIES>): DEXJPUS (USD/JPY noon-ET buying rate), DFF (US effective fed funds, daily), DGS2 (US 2y CMT, daily), IRSTCI01JPM156N (Japan overnight call/interbank rate, monthly), IR3TIB01JPM156N (Japan 3M TIBOR, monthly, robustness arm only), VIXCLS (VIX close, descriptive only). cot_jpy_legacy.csv: CFTC Commitments of Traders LEGACY futures-only, JAPANESE YEN contract, via Socrata (publicreporting.cftc.gov/resource/6dca-aqww.json). jgb_hist.csv/jgb_current.csv: MOF JGB constant-maturity yield curve, historical + current-year (mof.go.jp/jgbs/reference/interest_rate/data/jgbcm_all.csv + jgbcm.csv). mof_feio_daily.csv: MOF daily FX-intervention detail (mof.go.jp .../feio/foreign_exchange_intervention_operations.csv). See scripts/research_fx_carry.py and scripts/research_fx_fundamentals.py's pre-registration headers for the full sourcing and clock-alignment rationale.
retention: permanent snapshots for offline, reproducible reruns -- backtest_data/fred_*.csv are S5's snapshot (root level); backtest_data/fx_fundamentals_20260822/ is S6's dated snapshot directory (its own independent fred_* copies plus cot/jgb/mof). Neither is re-scraped in place once written.

DEXJPUS.meaning: USD/JPY noon buying rate in New York (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System)
DEXJPUS.notes: no row on days the rate is not published (weekends/US holidays) -- a calendar non-event, not a gap

DFF.meaning: US effective federal funds rate, daily

DGS2.meaning: US 2-year Treasury constant maturity rate, daily
DGS2.notes: '.' or blank on non-trading days per FRED convention

observation_date.meaning: observation month (FRED monthly series, stamped to a day)

IR3TIB01JPM156N.meaning: Japan 3-month TIBOR (interbank rate), monthly -- robustness-arm series only, not the primary JP short-rate leg

observation_date.meaning: observation month (FRED monthly series, stamped to a day)

IRSTCI01JPM156N.meaning: Japan immediate (<24h) call money / interbank rate, monthly -- the primary JP overnight short-rate leg used to match against US DFF

VIXCLS.notes: descriptive only in S6 -- not used as a trading-family input, per research_fx_fundamentals.py

report_date.notes: stamped Tuesday; released the following Friday -- see research_fx_fundamentals.py's pub_ts clock derivation before using this as an entry timestamp

market.meaning: exchange/contract label -- 'JAPANESE YEN - INTERNATIONAL MONETARY MARKET' (1986-01-15..2000-08-22) or 'JAPANESE YEN - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE' (2000-08-29..present); same underlying contract, non-overlapping date ranges

quality._notes: net non-commercial (nc_long - nc_short) is the derived feature actually used; positive = speculators net long the yen = net short USD/JPY, per research_fx_fundamentals.py

jgb_hist.csv._note: intentionally empty: see known_defects -- the real header (基準日,1年,2年,...40年, i.e. base-date + tenor columns) is TWO rows down from the file's actual first line and is Shift-JIS encoded, so what scripts/data_quality.py's UTF-8 reader sees as 'the header' (row 1) is really a Japanese title/units line, not column names.

jgb_current.csv._note: same structure/caveat as jgb_hist.csv -- current fiscal year's JGB yield curve, spliced onto jgb_hist.csv's history by scripts/research_fx_fundamentals.py's load_jgb_2y().

mof_feio_daily.csv._note: intentionally empty: see known_defects -- real per-row fields (positions 3/4/5/6/8, 0-indexed: year, month, day, amount in 100-million JPY, JPY-buy/sell side) are parsed positionally by scripts/research_fx_fundamentals.py's load_mof_interventions() directly from the Shift-JIS bytes; there is no single stable UTF-8 header row for this schema to declare.

known_defects: jgb_hist.csv, jgb_current.csv and mof_feio_daily.csv are Shift-JIS (cp932-family) encoded MOF downloads. scripts/data_quality.py (like scripts/intake_ledger.py) opens every file as UTF-8 with errors='replace', so their header/early rows decode into mojibake (replacement characters, stray CJK-adjacent bytes) rather than readable text -- this is a decoding artifact of the generic tooling, not file corruption. Only scripts/research_fx_fundamentals.py, which explicitly re-opens these three files with encoding='shift_jis', parses them correctly.

MOF publishes a MONTHLY TOTAL for FX intervention on the last business day of month M (covering (M-1)-27..M-26), and the DAILY breakdown only ~2 months after quarter end -- mof_feio_daily.csv's quarter-total rows are distinguishable only by an empty Day field, per research_fx_fundamentals.py; do not assume every row is a genuine single-day intervention record

Japanese-era date tokens in jgb_hist.csv/jgb_current.csv (S/H/R + 2-digit year, e.g. 'R8.8.3') require era-aware conversion (see research_fx_fundamentals.py's _jp_era_date) -- a naive date parse will misread or reject them

cot_jpy_legacy.csv cadence changes from BI-WEEKLY (until 1992-09-30) to WEEKLY (from 1992-10 onward), measured not assumed -- trading-family research restricts to report_date >= 1992-10-01 for this reason; the earlier bi-weekly rows are for descriptive/IC use only

fred_DEXJPUS.csv and fred_DGS2.csv exist independently in two places (backtest_data/ root, for S5, and backtest_data/fx_fundamentals_20260822/, for S6) -- fetched separately by design, so the two copies are not guaranteed to be byte-identical even though they cover the same FRED series
